description: pkix-path-builder/tests/bettertls.rs:78-87 — Observed::to_json formats string fields via Rust's Debug ({:?}) which differs from JSON encoding in edge cases: Rust escapes non-ASCII as \u{XXXX} (curly braces), JSON requires \uXXXX (no braces); tabs are \t in both but other control chars diverge. The baseline-pkix-path.json file is labeled as JSON but is parsed by load_baseline (line 234-280) with a hand-rolled brace-matching scanner that does not verify JSON syntax. The round-trip works because the SAME Debug-rendering is used to write and to read (each line's stored value is compared byte-for-byte). It will not work if anyone opens the file in a JSON tool and re-writes it (e.g., `jq . file > file` to format). The mislabeling is documented (line 240-243 calls out the hand-rolled scan rationale) but worth fixing to use proper JSON escaping. Suggested fix: a tiny json_escape helper, or accept the labeling mismatch and rename the file to .baseline-pkix-path.txt — at least then nobody passes it through jq. Minor; the test works as-is. Calling it out so future debugging doesn't waste time wondering why jq corrupts the baseline.
title: Observed::to_json uses Debug-quoting via {:?}, breaks if reasons contain unicode escapes or control chars
